newsitem.title: USA: El Al to use new bomb detector at New York airport.
newsitem.headline: El Al to use new bomb detector at New York airport.

text.p: Israel's El Al airline has ordered a new $1 million bomb-detection system for use at New York's John F. Kennedy international airport, the first carrier to do so, the manufacturer said on Monday.
InVision Technologies Inc said its CTX 5000 system, approved by the Federal Aviation Administration, was the fourth ordered by El Al. The others were installed in Israel.
The system was used in several European airports but had previously been tested in only two U.S. airports -- by Delta Air Lines in Atlanta and United Airlines in San Francisco.
"It's not integrated into their system at Kennedy yet but Israeli experts will be over to work on it and it should be up and running in about two weeks," InVision spokesman Langdon Cook said.
El Al spokeswoman Sheryl Stein confirmed that the airline had already received the system but declined to give further details.

InVision said its CTX 5000 system, using CAT-scanning, high quality X-rays and computer technology, provides quick and thorough detection of all categories of explosives, even when they are concealed in baggage.

The company announced the El Al decision on the same day President Bill Clinton called on Congress to provide $1 billion in funding to hire more FBI agents to fight terrorism and to broadly improve U.S. airline and airport security.
Investigators believe a bomb may have brought down TWA Flight 800 in July shortly after takeoff from Kennedy airport.
